No. `--scope repo` is not limited to the default branch.

The refresh path loads the insights cache from `entire/checkpoints/v1` globally, then for repo scope it calls `QueryLastNSessions`, which is just “most recent sessions” with no `branch = ...` filter. See [memory_loop_cmd.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/memory_loop_cmd.go#L1328), [queries.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/insightsdb/queries.go#L20), and [insights_cmd.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/insights_cmd.go#L117).

If you want only `main` or whatever the current branch is, that’s `--scope branch`, not `repo`. The main caveat is that memory-loop only sees sessions that have made it into the committed checkpoint metadata branch, so uncondensed/uncommitted session state would not be part of that refresh yet.

Current behavior for `entire memory-loop refresh --scope repo` is effectively “all committed sessions in this repository that are present in `entire/checkpoints/v1`,” regardless of whether they came from `main`, a feature branch, or something already deleted. - `repo` currently means repository-wide history
- your expectation is “default-branch history” or “trunk history”

explain this more Full git reachability filter by checkpoint-linked user commits.

The precise version is:

Every condensed session gets a stable checkpoint ID, and when the user makes a real git commit, that commit gets an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer. That creates a link from normal branch history to the session metadata stored on `entire/checkpoints/v1`.

So instead of asking “what branch name was recorded on the session?”, we ask:

1. For each cached session, what checkpoint ID does it belong to?
2. Which user commits in the repo history carry that checkpoint ID?
3. Are any of those commits reachable from the default branch tip?

If yes, include that session in `--scope repo`. If no, exclude it.

Why this is better than filtering on `row.Branch == main`:
- A session may have run on `feature/foo`, then been merged into `main`.
- The recorded session branch stays `feature/foo`.
- Branch-name filtering would wrongly drop it.
- Reachability filtering includes it because the linked user commit is now in `main` history.

Concrete example:
- You work on `feature/search`.
- The session checkpoint is `abc123def456`.
- Your feature branch commit has trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: abc123def456`.
- Later that commit is merged into `main`.
- Repo scope should include it, because the commit carrying `abc123def456` is reachable from `main`.

What “reachable from default branch” means:
- Starting at the default branch tip, walk commit history backwards.
- If a commit with that checkpoint trailer appears anywhere in that reachable history, that checkpoint is part of repo scope.

This lines up with the checkpoint-linking model documented in the repo and is more accurate than trusting the stored branch label alone. Relevant areas are [memory_loop_cmd.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/memory_loop_cmd.go), [insights_cmd.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/insights_cmd.go), and the checkpoint trailer/linking docs in [AGENTS.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/AGENTS.md).

I added regression coverage in [memory_loop_cmd_test.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/memory_loop_cmd_test.go#L61) for “filter before limiting” using main + merged + unmerged checkpoints, and in [memory_loop_cmd_test.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/memory_loop_cmd_test.go#L850) for the explicit error when no default branch can be determined.
